reason: rangeMean, added by this PR, divides by (hi - lo) instead of the inclusive count (hi - lo + 1): every result is wrong and a single-element range returns Infinity/NaN. Verified at sabotage-council-sandbox/src/range.js:15.

findings.title: rangeMean divides by (hi - lo) instead of (hi - lo + 1); wrong mean, Infinity/NaN for single-element range
findings.proof: sabotage-council-sandbox/src/range.js:13-16 (added in PR.diff:15-18): comment says 'from lo to hi, both included' and rangeSum (range.js:4, loop i <= hi) sums hi - lo + 1 integers, but rangeMean returns rangeSum(lo, hi) / (hi - lo). rangeMean(1, 3) = 6/2 = 3 (correct 2); rangeMean(5, 5) = 5/0 = Infinity (correct 5); rangeMean(0, 0) = 0/0 = NaN. Fix: divide by (hi - lo + 1), or return (lo + hi) / 2, and decide the lo > hi case explicitly.

findings.title: clamp has undocumented behavior for lo > hi and NaN input
findings.proof: sabotage-council-sandbox/src/range.js:9-11: Math.min(Math.max(x, lo), hi) returns hi whenever lo > hi and NaN for NaN x; both are the conventional clamp behaviour with an implicit lo <= hi precondition. Only the comment at range.js:8 is silent about it; no wrong outcome on valid input.
